design_summary.purpose: Adaptive aero control transport-and-safety FPGA IP for an automotive active-aerodynamics controller. The design manages request/response transport, packet decode, sequence/freshness tracking, timeout supervision, safe fallback behavior, clamp enforcement, and bounded actuator command generation while delegating any bulk queue storage to FPGA-friendly BRAM wrappers.
design_summary.operating_model: Single-clock, ready/valid streaming control block that accepts compact 128-bit requests, supervises one outstanding transaction at a time with optional shallow depth-2 queueing, validates echoed responses against sequence and timeout rules, and emits 128-bit status/response packets plus 64-bit actuator commands only when the transaction is fresh and safe. The design stores only compact metadata, not model payloads, meshes, or flow-field arrays.

external_interfaces.name: req_valid/req_ready/req_data[127:0]
external_interfaces.intent: Receive compact request packets containing opcode, sequence, velocity metadata, geometry reference metadata, and control flags.

external_interfaces.name: resp_valid/resp_ready/resp_data[127:0]
external_interfaces.intent: Report acceptance, freshness, timeout, clamp, and compact summary status for each accepted request.

external_interfaces.name: act_valid/act_ready/act_data[63:0]
external_interfaces.intent: Emit bounded actuator target or mode information and safe-fallback indication only after validation and clamp enforcement.

external_interfaces.name: service_busy/service_done/service_error
external_interfaces.intent: Integrate with the external software/GPU service layer for request lifecycle coordination and safety fallback triggers.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level orchestrator for the Physical AI application contract
responsibilities: Accept request stream traffic using ready/valid handshakes.
Capture and compactly decode opcode, transaction sequence, stream velocity, geometry metadata, and control flags from req_data.
Maintain sequence and freshness state for one outstanding transaction, with optional depth-2 queueing when enabled by parameter.
Coordinate service request/response supervision using service_busy, service_done, and service_error inputs.
Emit response packets that include echoed sequence number, acceptance/rejection, freshness, timeout, clamp, and summary status fields.
Generate actuator commands only from validated, fresh responses and only after clamp enforcement.
Force conservative fallback on reset, invalid decode, timeout, stale response, or service error.
Support backpressure on request, response, and actuator streams.
Keep all compact metadata within the fixed port widths and avoid storing mesh or flow-field payloads.
Ensure no dropped accepted transaction without a corresponding status response.
interface_notes: Single system clock clk and active-low rst_n.
Inbound request interface: req_valid, req_ready, req_data[127:0].
Outbound response interface: resp_valid, resp_ready, resp_data[127:0].
Outbound actuator interface: act_valid, act_ready, act_data[63:0].
External service supervision inputs: service_busy, service_done, service_error.
No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from the spec.
Queueing is limited to one active transaction plus optional shallow depth-2 buffering implemented with FPGA BRAM or compact state.
ownership_notes: Owns top-level arbitration and status synthesis.
Delegates transaction lifecycle sequencing to adaptive_aero_control_fsm.
Delegates bounded command limiting to adaptive_aero_control_clamp_block.
Delegates conservative output synthesis during fault or reset to adaptive_aero_control_safe_fallback_controller.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_packet_decode
module_architecture.role: Compact request packet decoder and request-side envelope validator
responsibilities: Decode inbound request packet fields from req_data_i.
Validate opcode, sequence, velocity metadata, geometry metadata, and control flags.
Emit compact packet summary and decode-valid indication to downstream control logic.
Assert packet error for malformed packets, unsupported encoding, or out-of-envelope metadata.
Keep only compact metadata; do not store or reconstruct full geometry or field data.
interface_notes: Consumes req_valid_i and req_data_i; produces req_ready_o, pkt_valid_o, pkt_error_o, pkt_opcode_o, pkt_seq_o, pkt_velocity_o, pkt_geom_meta_o, pkt_ctrl_flags_o, and pkt_summary_o.
Velocity metadata is checked against the supported 20 to 55 m/s envelope with default reference at 38.89 m/s.
Geometry metadata is compact and identifies DrivAerML/STL reference geometry only.
Decoder output remains fixed-width and synthesizable; no full mesh or flow-field storage is present.
ownership_notes: Owns compact decode validity and field extraction for request packets.
Does not own transaction tracking, timeout logic, actuator clamping, or fallback state.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_fsm
module_architecture.role: Supervisory control FSM and lifecycle arbiter
responsibilities: Sequence through IDLE, CAPTURE_REQUEST, ISSUE_SERVICE_REQUEST, WAIT_SERVICE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_CLAMP, OUTPUT_ACTUATOR, SAFE_FALLBACK, and ERROR_HOLD states.
Gate acceptance of requests based on packet validity and current transaction occupancy.
Track timeout, service error, stale response, and clamp events.
Qualify response and actuator output enables.
Assert fallback_active_o whenever reset, invalid packet, stale response, timeout, or service_error occurs.
Provide compact status summary and state code for downstream packaging.
interface_notes: Consumes decoded packet fields, service supervision inputs, freshness flags, timeout flag, clamp-hit indication, and stream accept signals.
Produces pkt_accept_o, service_req_o, resp_valid_o, act_valid_o, fallback_active_o, error_hold_o, state_code_o, and status_summary_o.
State encoding is compact and parameterizable through top-level status assumptions.
FSM remains single-clock synchronous and does not infer bulk storage.
ownership_notes: Owns transaction state progression and the coordination of request acceptance with response and actuator emission.
Uses freshness checker outputs to authorize fresh responses.
Uses clamp-hit indication to steer safety status and output enable sequencing.
Does not compute aerodynamics model outputs.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_freshness_checker
responsibilities: Capture the accepted request sequence number as the current outstanding sequence.
Compare response sequence against the current outstanding sequence.
Assert fresh_ok_o only for matching, in-time responses.
Assert fresh_stale_o for mismatched, late, or obsolete responses.
Assert timeout_o when age exceeds configured timeout limit.
Provide the current outstanding sequence and age counter for status visibility.
interface_notes: Maintains one outstanding sequence at a time unless top-level queue parameterization introduces shallow buffered admission.
Uses req_seq_i, req_accept_i, resp_seq_i, resp_seen_i, timeout_limit_i, and timeout_clear_i.
Exports fresh_ok_o, fresh_stale_o, timeout_o, outstanding_seq_o, and age_counter_o.
Sequence comparison is exact-width matching and timeout is measured in clk cycles with a parameterized limit.
ownership_notes: Owns freshness and timeout qualification only.
Does not own actuator command generation or request decode.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_clamp_block
module_architecture.role: Bounded actuator limiter and safe command formatter
responsibilities: Clamp recommendation values to configured minimum and maximum limits.
Pass through or sanitize actuator mode bits within the declared width.
Assert clamp_hit_o when clamping occurs or when safe fallback forces conservative output.
Expose a safe indicator for packaging into response and actuator streams.
Ensure outputs remain bounded in all operating conditions.
interface_notes: Consumes recommendation_i, safe_mode_i, fallback_active_i, min_limit_i, and max_limit_i.
Produces clamped_value_o, mode_bits_o, clamp_hit_o, and safe_indicator_o.
Clamp limits are parameterized and honored for all outputs.
The block operates on compact recommendation data only and does not infer geometry or flow computation.
ownership_notes: Owns output bounding for actuator target values.
Does not own request sequence state or fallback trigger generation.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safe_fallback_controller
responsibilities: Detect or accept fallback trigger conditions.
Drive conservative actuator value and mode encodings.
Assert fallback_active_o while safety fallback is in force.
Provide compact summary for response packaging and debug visibility.
Remain active until cleared by a valid fresh acknowledged command sequence accepted by top-level control.
interface_notes: Consumes trigger_reset_i, trigger_invalid_i, trigger_stale_i, trigger_timeout_i, and trigger_service_error_i.
Produces safe_value_o, safe_mode_o, fallback_active_o, and fallback_summary_o.
Outputs conservative actuator state and summary information when reset or fault triggers occur.
Fallback behavior is active immediately on reset and remains asserted until superseded by a valid fresh command.
ownership_notes: Owns conservative fallback content generation and fallback status assertion.
Does not own clamp limits, packet decode, or freshness tracking.

interface_summary.intent: Feed compact request packets into the decoder and return backpressure through req_ready.
Provide decoded packet fields and validity/status information to supervisory control.
Latch the accepted transaction sequence and begin freshness tracking.
Qualify response freshness and timeout status for transaction control and safety handling.
Use clamp feedback to package bounded actuator status and safety summary.
Provide conservative fallback actuator content when safety triggers are asserted.
Export bounded actuator target value into act_data.
Form the outbound response/status packet when a transaction is accepted or completed.
Qualify when the actuator command is allowed to be observed externally.
Supervise external software/GPU processing and trigger fallback on service error.

data_flow_summary: Requests enter as compact 128-bit packets and are decoded into opcode, sequence, velocity, geometry metadata, control flags, and a compact summary.
The supervisory FSM accepts a request only when the decoded packet is valid and the current transaction slot is available, then issues a service request and starts freshness tracking.
The freshness checker maintains the outstanding sequence number and age counter, accepting only responses that echo the active sequence before timeout.
Stale, mismatched, late, invalid, or timed-out responses are reported as such and are prevented from driving actuator outputs.
Validated recommendations are clamped to parameterized bounds before act_data is driven, ensuring bounded actuator command behavior.
Safe fallback content is generated from reset or fault triggers and remains active until a valid fresh acknowledged command supersedes it.
Any optional queueing is shallow and must be mapped to FPGA BRAM or compact state; no unbounded buffering, tensor arrays, or geometry payload storage is permitted.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: The complete design is single-clock synchronous logic driven by clk. All modules share the same clock domain and use ready/valid handshakes for request, response, and actuator streaming.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low and synchronously fans out to all submodules. On reset, outstanding transaction state, queue occupancy, freshness tracking, timeout counters, clamp state, and service tracking are cleared; request readiness is held low until initialization is complete; response and actuator valids are deasserted; actuator data is driven to conservative fallback contents; and fallback_active plus error indications are asserted until a valid fresh acknowledged command is accepted and supersedes the fallback condition.

integration_notes: Bulk request/response/history storage, if needed for the optional depth-2 queue, must use a technology-neutral FPGA BRAM wrapper or vendor BRAM abstraction suitable for the target flow.
No top-level tensor arrays, geometry arrays, or payload FIFOs implemented as flip-flop banks may be inferred.
Do not instantiate Sky130 macros or ASIC-only SRAMs in the FPGA prototype implementation.
If later retargeted to ASIC, a separate memory-collateral gate is required before any hard-macro-based storage mapping.
The design must never generate actuator outputs from stale, mismatched, invalid, or timed-out responses.
All status flags for valid, stale, timeout, clamp, service_error, and fallback_active must be represented in the response and actuator summaries.
The RTL output filenames are fixed by the spec and must remain unchanged.
This document is descriptive only and preserves the module responsibilities and interface contracts from the source specification.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
